_doc: TSUGE dating cabinet (#41, Wave E, built 2026-07-17-eve; roster #48 — the JAPANESE school opener). Kyoichiro Tsuge's house: workshop founded 1936 (ivory pipes/cigarette holders first), cherry pipes from 1945, BRIAR from the 1950s, European-trained freehand era from the 1970s. SOURCES: staging/pipedia/Tsuge.json (company catalog history via Uekusa/Poggenpohl) + Beyond_Tsuge.json (smokingpipes, 16KB — partially mined; Ikebana noted).

history_anchors._doc: Kyoichiro Tsuge b.1911 (Kanazawa; swordsmith/samurai lineage). Orphaned 13; apprenticed under a master IVORY pipe maker (Tokyo) from 1924. 1936: opens TSUGE PIPE COMPANY Ltd. WWII: factory makes wooden gun stocks; Kyoichiro sent to war. 1945: restart — ivory unobtainable (GHQ control) -> CHERRY WOOD (Tohoku) cigarette holders, then pipes (the MacArthur corncob landing + US pipe tobacco = the boom); umbrella-handle craftsmen hired; billiards/bent billiards mass-produced; 120 craftsmen at peak. 1950s: imported BRIAR arrives -> briar pipes; carved souvenir bowls for US soldiers (Mt. Fuji, three monkeys, Toshogu, Geisha; sold at Imperial Hotel/PX/USO). 1960s: Vietnam-war soldier demand; cherry pipes exported to Saigon. 1970s: yen crisis -> pivot to high-value: six craftsmen sent to Italy+Denmark; FUKADO + SATO study under SIXTEN IVARSSON and JØRGEN LARSEN (Danish-school graft — artisan registry links!) -> freehands to the US, then Germany/Switzerland success. Ikebana = the high-grade line (Beyond Tsuge covers the modern era — future mine).

brand_marks.physical: Era tells by MATERIAL: ivory = pre-war/earliest; cherry wood = 1945+ (mainstay to the 60s; Saigon exports); briar = 1950s+; Danish-influenced freehands = 1970s+. Carved traditional-motif bowls (Fuji/monkeys/Geisha) = 1950s-60s souvenir era.
